sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Cryo-EM structure of MAS1 was obtained with the tag in place, demonstrating that the tagged full-length receptor was expressed, purified, and correctly folded; no explicit signaling or binding functional assay is reported in the cited clip.
sites.rationale: L1 reports an N-terminal HA tag on full-length membrane-anchored MAS1, a Mas-related GPCR paralog of MAS1L; this counts as indirect evidence. MAS1L topology landmarks show residues 1–76 are extracellular with no signal peptide, making the N-terminus the only extracellular terminus and the prepend position (insert_after_residue=0, residue_after=M) the unique topology-derived junction. Python verification confirms seq[1]=M and TM1 begins at residue 77, placing the prepend 77 residues from any TM boundary, well beyond the ≥3-residue minimum. No residue number is named in L1 for MAS1L, so position_evidence is topology_derived, not validated. Full-length, membrane-anchored MAS1 (Mas1 receptor, a close paralog of MAS1L in the Mas-related GPCR subfamily) was engineered with an N-terminal HA epitope tag plus 6×His and bRIL for cryo-EM expression and purification. MAS1L has no signal peptide (topology landmarks place residue 1 as extracellular), so the sole extracellular terminus is the N-terminus; a prepend (insert_after_residue=0) is the only position consistent with 'N-terminal' on the extracellular face.

sources.claim: To enable efficient expression and purification, we engineered the wild-type full-length Mas1 receptor with an N-terminal hemagglutinin (HA) epitope tag, a 6×His tag for affinity purification, and a bRIL fusion tag.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) is available. It reports an N-terminal HA tag on full-length MAS1 (Mas1 receptor, PMC13187490), a paralog of MAS1L in the Mas-related GPCR subfamily; it does not report any tag on MAS1L itself. The evidence is therefore indirect and the position topology-derived. No ledger line grounds any internal extracellular loop (ECL1 132–147, ECL2 214–221, ECL3 287–296) or the intracellular C-terminus (318–378) of MAS1L. The bRIL fusion mentioned in L1 is a thermostabilizing insert commonly placed in ICL3 of GPCRs; because the clip does not specify its position and ICL3 is intracellular, no additional site is proposed. Confidence is low because the sole supporting evidence is from a paralog, not MAS1L itself.
